title: Utility shutoff, payee named PG&E but new account, prepaid card

conversation.speaker: caller
conversation.text: This is PG&E disconnection services. Your account is past due and a technician is scheduled to shut off your power within the hour.

conversation.speaker: margaret
conversation.text: I paid the bill last week. I have the receipt.

conversation.speaker: caller
conversation.text: The payment did not post. To stop the shutoff today you must pay four hundred eighty by prepaid card right now. Our normal billing office cannot stop the truck, only this department can.

conversation.speaker: margaret
conversation.text: I have medicine in the refrigerator. I cannot lose power.

conversation.speaker: caller
conversation.text: Then stay on the line and pay now.

review_note: signals_required. Beneficiary name exactly matches a known biller, so A-01 would ALLOW even though the account_ref is new. Only urgency plus new payee (H-04) or shutoff threat (H-06) holds it. Name-match alone should not confer known-biller status. With ref-only known-biller matching, A-01 cannot fire for a new ref even though the name is PG&E; default HOLD applies even with zero signals.
